values: Read PDF provides online and offline PDF reading for the selected document. It renders the PDF, restores the last read page, supports page navigation, zoom and fit controls, displays the document outline when available, automatically stores reading progress, and provides device-specific offline actions including Save for offline, Read offline and Remove offline copy.
SCR-05 reader design and control-state specification for Contents and offline actions.
Overview of PDF loading, reading progress, navigation and offline actions.
Open SCR-05 with the selected Book ID when the user chooses Read or Resume Reading.
The reader may be opened from MD-01, Library, Recent, Favourite or Dashboard.
Display a loading state while resolving the PDF source and loading document metadata.
Reader controls are disabled until the PDF is ready.
Resolve the PDF using this priority: IndexedDB offline copy, application-managed LOCAL_UPLOAD copy, then REMOTE_URL.
If the browser is offline, REMOTE_URL cannot be used unless an IndexedDB copy exists.
If no accessible source exists or PDF loading fails, display an error with Retry and Back actions.
Do not display an empty reader as a successful state.
Display the selected document title and author in the header.
The design text “Medication” should be corrected if the actual title is “Meditations”.
When Back is selected, save reading progress and return to the origin screen.
Although the mockup says Back to Library, returning to the actual origin is recommended.
Display common navigation according to the desktop layout.
Do not incorrectly highlight Favorites unless it is the origin/current navigation context.
After the PDF loads, open lastReadPage; if it is unavailable or invalid, open page 1.
Render the selected PDF page inside the reader area.
Show a per-page loading indicator when rendering takes noticeable time.
Move to the previous page when Previous is selected.
Move to the next page when Next is selected.
Display current page and total pages in the format PAGE X OF Y.
The current page must update after every navigation action.
Allow the user to enter a page number and navigate after Enter or confirmation.
Reject non-numeric values and values outside 1–totalPages.
Support Page Up/Page Down or arrow-key navigation when focus is not inside an input.
Do not override browser shortcuts unexpectedly.
Decrease the zoom level when Zoom Out is selected.
Increase the zoom level when Zoom In is selected.
Disable when the maximum zoom level is reached.
Default value may be 100% or Fit Width according to product decision.
Toggle or select a fit mode such as Fit Width or Fit Page.
The icon between zoom and page navigation requires a tooltip because its meaning is not self-evident.
Enable Contents only when the PDF contains a usable outline/table of contents.
Display the disabled state shown in the control specification when no outline exists.
When Contents is selected, open a side panel or popover containing the PDF outline.
Keep the current page visible where possible.
When an outline item is selected, close or retain the panel according to responsive rules and navigate to its destination page.
Update current page and reading progress.
Automatically save lastReadPage and lastReadAt when the current page changes.
Use debounce to avoid excessive API calls; also flush on Back or page unload when possible.
If progress saving fails, keep reading available and retry silently or show a non-blocking warning.
Do not interrupt PDF reading for a temporary progress-sync error.
Enable Read offline when an offline PDF copy is available on the current browser/device.
Offline availability is determined from IndexedDB or equivalent application-managed local storage.
Disable Read offline when no offline copy exists.
Use the disabled state shown in the control specification and provide a tooltip explaining how to save the PDF offline.
When selected, load the PDF from the offline copy and continue from the current or last read page.
No network connection is required after the local copy has been resolved.
When the More icon is selected, display Download PDF, Save for offline and Remove offline copy actions.
Each action's enabled state depends on source and offline availability.
Download a copy of the PDF through the browser/device download mechanism.
This action creates a user-managed file and does not by itself update application Offline Status.
Save the PDF to IndexedDB for application-managed offline reading.
Enable when no IndexedDB copy exists and a downloadable source is accessible.
While saving for offline, display progress and prevent duplicate operations.
The reader may remain usable if technically safe.
After saving succeeds, enable Read offline, disable Save for offline and enable Remove offline copy.
Offline state is browser- and device-specific.
On failure, remove incomplete IndexedDB data and display Retry.
Do not modify sourceType or delete the original source.
Remove the application-managed IndexedDB copy after user confirmation.
Do not delete the Book record, user-managed downloaded file or remote source.
After removal, disable Read offline, enable Save for offline and update Offline Status.
If another application-managed local source remains available, recompute availability before disabling.
For a REMOTE_URL document without an IndexedDB copy: enable Download PDF and Save for offline; disable Remove offline copy and Read offline.
Requires an online connection to execute Download or Save.
For a REMOTE_URL document with an IndexedDB copy: enable Download PDF, Read offline and Remove offline copy; disable Save for offline.
Download PDF remains available because it serves a different user-managed purpose.
For LOCAL_UPLOAD, enable actions according to actual application-managed availability.
If the PDF is already stored for offline reading, enable Read offline and Remove offline copy; Save for offline is disabled.
When online, allow remote loading and all actions whose source requirements are satisfied.
Display Online Mode in the footer.
When offline, load only an available local/offline copy and disable network-dependent actions.
Display Offline Mode and a clear reason when the document is unavailable.
On mobile, collapse navigation, maximize the reading area and keep essential controls reachable without horizontal page scrolling.
Secondary actions may remain inside the More menu.
Provide keyboard focus, accessible names and tooltips for icon-only controls and disabled-state explanations.
Announce page changes and loading errors appropriately.
Render pages on demand and release unnecessary page resources when appropriate.
Avoid loading and rendering all pages simultaneously for large PDFs.
